sentences.text: Few cranial elements are preserved, including a premaxilla with a strongly hooked tip similar to other phorusrhacids. The humerus is heavily curved with an almost elliptical shaft, while the ulna is notably more atrophied than that of Mesembriornis.

The preserved vertebral column includes thirteen cervical vertebrae arranged in an S-curve with strong curvature in the upper section. The tarsometatarsus is notably short, measuring only half the length of the long, robust tibiotarsus. The anterior and superior portions of the pelvis are preserved, showing an iliac crest similar to Psilopterus and Mesembriornis.

Nearly the entire left wing and some right wing elements are preserved, showing wings heavily reduced even more than in other phorusrhacids. Unlike other phorusrhacids, Paraphysornis lacks preserved quill knobs, suggesting its feathers were not as strongly anchored.

The only known fossil of Paraphysornis is a nearly complete skeleton discovered between 1977 and 1978. Excavation yielded a 75% complete skeleton that lacked most of the cranium, pelvis, and sternum.
The mandible anatomy and claw shape indicate that Paraphysornis was a carnivore like other phorusrhacids. Unable to chase fast prey, Paraphysornis likely hunted using ambush tactics or scavenging.

The genus name Paraphysornis combines the name Physornis with the Greek suffix "para-" to mean "close to Physornis". Paraphysornis is traditionally classified in the subfamily Brontornithinae alongside Brontornis and Physornis. Agnolin proposed the subfamily name Physornithinae for a clade containing Physornis and Paraphysornis.

Paraphysornis lived around 23 million years ago during the Late Oligocene to Early Miocene in what is now southern Brazil. Paraphysornis lived in the Tremembé Formation, which preserves evidence of a shallow lake environment. The time range for Paraphysornis is estimated from 27.3 to 23.04 million years ago.
